title: Learning research
summary: What the app does because research on memory and second-language learning supports it.
description: Polski is designed from what research on memory and on learning a second language finds works. Each requirement names the finding, briefly with its source, and states what the app does because of it.

stories.as: an adult learning Polish in spare minutes
stories.want: my practice to be the kind that research shows makes words stick
stories.soThat: the minutes I have turn into Polish I keep

stories.as: a learner whose first language is English
stories.want: practice pitched at what I am ready for, with help where English misleads me
stories.soThat: I make progress instead of guessing

requirements.text: Spaced practice: each lesson comes back on its own schedule, with gaps that grow as it is passed again after longer.
Spacing over cramming: the last stretch to mastered needs a pass on a second day, and a pass after a longer gap earns more mastery points.
Each word and sentence has spaced reviews of its own, and answering it more than once in a day counts once.
Retrieval practice (the testing effect): a word or sentence is only read on a card the first time; after that every card asks the learner to recall or recognise it.
Receptive before productive (Nation): a word's or sentence's cards go from recognising it to producing it, a step up for each day it is answered without a miss and a step down after a day with one.

Processability (Pienemann): the learner chooses a word's ending, such as a noun's case or a verb's person, only from A2, between two forms, and from every form only from B1; at A1 a sentence's endings are given and only its order is built.
Comprehensible input (Krashen): the tutor keeps a course's core lessons at the course's level and marks a lesson beyond it a challenge, and a writing partner writes at its lesson's level.
Desirable difficulties (Bjork) near the 85% success sweet spot (Wilson and others): a drill passes at `drill.pass-share` right, and its cards harden as its items become known.
Partial credit: an answer one slip off is almost right and counts as `drill.almost-share` right, and a go short of a pass earns a share of mastery points.
Immediate corrective feedback: a scored card is judged as soon as it is answered, and a miss is shown with the right answer, which is also read aloud.
Worked examples on a miss: a word answered wrong is shown in example sentences.
A miss is answered by more practice, not a penalty: it brings the lesson or the item back sooner, and takes no points away.
Interleaving: a drill mixes kinds of card, each item on the card its own familiarity gives, and a words lesson asks the words met before in a shuffled order.

Minimal-pair training for sounds an English ear runs together (such as sz and ś): words and sentences lessons have a round of sound pairs built from their own words, and a spoken word heard as its pair is named by the sound confused.
Dual coding (Paivio): concrete words can be learnt from a drawing of each, and a place's words where the things are in one drawing of it.
Relevance: every course is built on what the learner asked to learn Polish for.
Retrieval after mastery: a mastered lesson's words still come back now and then as a light review.
Pushed output (Swain): a writing lesson has the learner get a point across to a partner who understands only Polish, with help that steps back after each pass.
